page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated compute instance designed for graphics-intensive computing and machine learning tasks. The configuration features 20 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 12.8 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a collective total of 96 GB of VRAM. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and the environment operates under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations position the system in the top tier for processor and memory throughput. Geekbench results show top-decile execution with single-core marks of 2,814 and multi-core scores reaching 22,204, reinforced by stress-ng metrics that sit in the top 10% for single-core output. Hardware vector capabilities are broad, including AVX-512, VNNI, and bfloat16 instruction sets. Large-block uncached read memory bandwidth exceeds 308 GB/s, while language model inference tests demonstrate 4,555.72 tokens per second in prompt processing on small 135M parameter models and 37.36 tokens per second in text generation on 7B models.

A notable hardware tradeoff is the total absence of integrated local storage, requiring workloads to rely on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. From a resource perspective, the high RAM-to-CPU ratio coupled with dual high-memory GPUs allows consolidation of parallel computing tasks without moving to dedicated host configurations. The architecture is well calibrated for generative AI inference, batch image and text processing pipelines, 3D rendering jobs, and data science workloads requiring substantial GPU memory footprints.
description: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated instance configured with 20 AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs, 256 GB of RAM, and dual NVIDIA L40S graphics processors delivering 96 GB of combined VRAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 vector instruction support, the host demonstrates top-tier single-core and multi-core benchmark rankings in Geekbench and stress-ng evaluations. The system excels at memory-heavy parallel computations, posting uncached read throughput exceeding 308 GB/s and strong inference processing speeds across compact language models. Because the instance includes no local storage drives, persistence depends entirely on external network volumes. The combination of dense host memory, 12.8 GB of RAM per vCPU, and dual Ada Lovelace accelerators positions this platform effectively for machine learning inference, computer vision, 3D rendering pipelines, and data-intensive analytical processing workloads.
